- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days, especially if price is trending up.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–4 days after peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often overfits short-term momentum; apply “sentiment-weighted smoothing”: average sentiment score with 0.7–0.9 weight to adjust forecast mean.
- If recent history shows high volatility (e.g., >3% daily swings), model tends to overpredict; apply “volatility dampening”: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per 1% volatility in history.
